original_question: Let L*_n be the height of the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n), meaning the maximum number of edges from the root to a leaf. Show that L*_n / log^2 n converges in probability to a constant c, and determine the value of c.
target_in_paper: Section 6.6, Open Problem 7 (“The height of DTCS(n)”) in the July 2024 v2 PDF of arXiv:2303.02529, whose wording matches your draft essentially exactly. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.02529))
correct_elements: Your draft already has the right model (the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n)), the right extremal statistic L_n^* (maximum root-to-leaf edge count), the right scale ((log n)^2), and the right mode of convergence (in probability). ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
missing_details: DTCS(n) should be defined explicitly: a clade of size m>=2 is split into subclades of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i)=m/[2 h_{m-1} i(m-i)] for 1<=i<=m-1, where h_{m-1}=sum_{j=1}^{m-1} 1/j. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

State explicitly that n tends to infinity and that log is the natural logarithm. The paper’s asymptotic formulas for DTCS heights use (log n)^2, not log base 2. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, distinguish L_n^* from L_n: L_n is the height of a uniform random leaf in DTCS(n), whereas L_n^* is the tree height. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

The paper presents this as an open problem/conjectural asymptotic, not as a proved theorem. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

Nearby context sharpening the scope is omitted: the paper recalls E[L_n]~3 pi^{-2}(log n)^2 and reports a known upper-tail bound P(L_n^*>beta (log n)^2)->0 for beta>beta_0≈0.93. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))

The paper does not state a proved value of c; it only suggests, from the greedy-path discussion and the lower bound coming from E[L_n], that c may be 3/pi^2. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
refined_question: For the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n), recursively constructed on the leaf set [n]={1,...,n} by splitting each clade of size m>=2 into subclades of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i)=m/[2 h_{m-1} i(m-i)] for 1<=i<=m-1, where h_{m-1}=sum_{j=1}^{m-1} 1/j, let L_n^* denote the tree height, i.e. the maximum number of edges on a path from the root to a leaf. Show that, as n->infinity, there exists a constant c such that L_n^*/(log n)^2 -> c in probability, and identify the constant c (with log denoting the natural logarithm). ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s DTCS tree-height conjecture: after defining L_n^* and L_n for the discrete model, section 6.6 states Open Problem 7 exactly as “Show that L_n^* ~ c log^2 n in probability, and identify the constant c.” The nearby context explains why this is the intended scale: earlier the paper records the DTCS leaf-height asymptotic E[L_n]~3 pi^{-2}(log n)^2, while section 6.6 notes a known upper bound P(L_n^*>beta (log n)^2)->0 for beta>beta_0≈0.93 and then remarks that greedy-path numerics suggest c may equal the lower bound 3/pi^2. ([storage.googleapis.com](https://storage.googleapis.com/arxiv-dataset/arxiv/arxiv/pdf/2303/2303.02529v2.pdf))
